<t>Dynamic models are the future of financial modelling. They respond to changes in business, competition, economics, supply chains, project deadlines and more. Excel’s dynamic arrays make this practical. But dynamic arrays are not possible in Financial Models without LAMBDA and LAMBDAs are too scary for most modellers. That’s where Ozzit steps in.</t>
<t>Ozzit makes it easy for anyone, including Excel novices, to assemble expert level financial models with dynamic arrays in record time with fewer errors!</t>

<t>Ozzit functions can be used exactly like native Excel functions because they are made from native Excel functions and nothing else. That means no special skills are required to use Ozzit functions and models assembled from Ozzit functions can be saved as normal .xlsx workbooks.</t>

<t xml:space="preserve">With a few exceptions, all Ozzit functions have inline help. Inline help explains the function's syntax, purpose, version, and arguments. To access a function's inline help, find an empty space on a worksheet and enter = and the function's name without any arguments. </t>

<t xml:space="preserve">Some Ozzit functions have Data Validation functions associated with them. These functions diagnose problems with arguments we present to their parent Ozzit function. So if a function returns an error or something unexpected, try calling its data validation routine which will attempt to diagnose any problems with the arguments. Data Validation functions are named using the function's name plus DV. As an example, we have a Ozzit function called Depreciateλ(). Depreciateλ's data validation function is DepreciateλDV(<include arguments>). </t>
